subject: Econ alignment & rollback clauses for price-match swap
messages:
From: Sarah Bloom <sarah.bloom@nebulacorp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: alignment / rollback language for competitor price match

Jonas —

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Nebula is evaluating a move from our current vendor (EdgeScale) and they came back with a last‑offer price that matches Redwood's headline rates but with a 12‑month locked term and an aggressive egress rebate. Procurement wants to understand:

- Whether Redwood can match the unit economics (per‑token + inference-minutes) and how that impacts typical ramp credits.
- Whether we can shape contract language to include a rollback (price protection) if resource utilization drops and they ask for retroactive credits.

I've attached EdgeScale's quote — you'll see their 30% first‑year discount plus a 6‑month migration credit and a 90‑day rollback clause. We need: a simple comparison and a recommended negotiation posture from Redwood (match + shorter rollback? credits instead of retro refunds?).

Can you and your pricing lead put together a one‑pager and recommended contract language by EOD next Friday (8/30)? Procurement will want suggested fallback options if Redwood can't match one line item.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Bloom
Head of Procurement, NebulaCorp
[sent from mobile]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Bloom <sarah.bloom@nebulacorp.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: alignment / rollback language for competitor price match

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the context and the quote. I've reviewed the PDF (thanks) and sketched the high‑level position below. Lauren and Ben are looped in for legal and commercial checks.

Quick read / suggested posture:
- Economics: We can match headline per‑token rates for the first 12 months if Nebula commits to a 12‑month minimum commit that approximates the quoted seat/throughput baseline. We prefer to frame this as a committed capacity credit rather than an upfront rebate; that preserves runway for capacity planning.
- Migration credits: we can offer a front‑loaded migration credit (equivalent to ~8% of first‑year committed spend) applied to invoice offsets for months 1–3 to cover integration and validation.
- Rollback language: Redwood is open to a limited price protection clause but with guardrails: 1) triggers only if utilization drops >40% vs committed baseline for two consecutive months; 2) rollback window capped at 60 days and rolling forward (no retro refunds beyond the 60‑day window); 3) both parties agree on usage measurement methodology (token definitions, sampling).
- Fallbacks: If we cannot match one element (e.g., egress rebate), propose a time‑limited addendum: we provide a temporary egress credit applied as invoice offsets for months 1–6 rather than a perpetual rebate.

Deliverables by 8/30: Lauren will draft recommended contract clause language and Ben will produce a short TCO comparison (monthly burn + 12‑month committed spend) showing the matched offer vs EdgeScale. I'll package this into a one‑pager for Procurement.

Couple of quick asks for Nebula to accelerate things:
1) Confirm the committed baseline (RPS/peak tokens/day) EdgeScale used to price the quote.
2) Confirm whether the 90‑day rollback is triggered by vendor downgrades or customer usage drops (the quote is ambiguous).

If you want a quick call Thursday to align, I'm available 10–11 PDT.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555‑0199

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: alignment / rollback language for competitor price match

Jonas —

Drafting contract language now. High‑level legal notes:
- We should avoid 'retroactive refund' language. Anything that suggests credits beyond a short reconciliation window is risky from a revenue recognition perspective.
- Proposed clause: "Price Protection" limited to adjustments to future invoices within a 60‑day reconciliation period and contingent on usage evidence mutually agreed upon. No cash refunds.
- Measurement: include explicit token counting spec + sample interval (UTC daily aggregates) and an audit path (limited to file exports and logs).
- Termination carveout: if Nebula terminates for convenience within first 6 months, migration credits are forfeited. That should discourage opportunistic churn.

Ben — can you build the quick TCO table with the following columns: EdgeScale quoted vs Redwood matched (committed rate, effective first‑year blended cost, migration credit applied, net first‑year cash out)? Keep assumptions visible. I can take the legal text and produce a redline for their commercial team.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Contracts & Commercial
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Bloom <sarah.bloom@nebulacorp.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: alignment / rollback language for competitor price match

Sarah — attaching the short TCO (spreadsheet exported as PDF) and the one‑pager with suggested contract language. Key takeaways up front:
- With a 12‑month commit at the matched per‑token rate, Redwood's net first‑year cash out (after a one‑time migration credit equal to ~8% of committed spend) is within ~2% of EdgeScale's quoted number.
- Our rollback proposal reduces Redwood's downside exposure while giving Nebula a clear reconciliation path; it also avoids the accounting complications of retroactive refunds.
- If Nebula needs the egress credit line item, we recommend the time‑limited invoice offset (months 1–6) vs an ongoing percentage rebate.

Attachments: Nebula_Competitive_Quote_0825.pdf (their quote), NB-2297_TCO_match_0826.pdf (our TCO), NB-2297_onepager_0826.pdf (contract language + recommended posture).

Next steps: Jonas to schedule a procurement-level call; if procurement wants any redlines, Lauren will handle the initial redline and legal loop.

Thanks — and happy to jump on a call later today if helpful.

—Ben
